newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs weak, little volume seen at monthly auction.
newsitem.headline: OLOs weak, little volume seen at monthly auction.

text.p: Belgian linear government bonds (OLOs) started lower with Bunds on very thin Monday trade ahead of the monthly OLO auction where little volume is expected.

Dealers said that an exceptionaly high 60 billion francs worth of OLOs sold at last week's exchange auction should have covered most of the Treasury's financing needs. They did not expect high demand from investors following heavy OLO sales by a large domestic player last week.
The Treasury is selling the June 2002 and March 2007 lines. Both are already very liquid, with outstanding amounts of 330 and 161 billion respectively.
One trader said there was little activity in the market, and that even in the bonds up for auction, there was hardly any of the short selling which is so common ahead of an auction.
The benchmark 10-year March 2007 OLO was quoted with a yield of 5.65 percent, from 5.62 percent on Friday, an unchanged 10 bp over equivalent Bunds.
"The sales by (a large domestic bank) have pushed the spread from six to 10 bp, the market has not quite recovered from that. Traders are still licking their wounds," one dealer said.
OLO futures were down 11 bp at 122.90 with just 98 lots traded.
